correctness.rationale: Every Rips simplex is either in a uniquely centered closed-neighborhood core or one of two alternating exceptional triangular faces per complete hexagon. The centered core collapses rel graph by unique distance-two midpoints. Attaching the first 2-cell of each pair forms a planar finite hexagon subcomplex, collapsible through free outer edges to a graph of cycle rank b-h; it gives independent primitive face-boundary classes. Remaining cells are null-attached, adding exactly h two-spheres. All claims use internal graph distances and handle arbitrary edge/vertex subgraphs, including bridges and one-vertex case. Exact clique enumeration and mod-two homology were independently recomputed for 151 finite instances; these are not proofs of infinite or integral claims.

originality.rationale: Full-text comparison with the periodic honeycomb and edge-disjoint hexagon results confirms that neither implies arbitrary finite subgraphs with edge-sharing hexagons, primitive integral H1 kernel, or the sharp shared-bond defect law. All-overlaps line-graph Rips results are for a distinct metric graph. Existing centered-core methodology is credited; an unindexed broader coverage theorem remains possible.
residual_risks: The finite-lattice argument shares local centered-core ideas with the 2026 periodic honeycomb theorem; an unindexed universal planar-hexagon lemma could subsume the stated result.

value.rationale: A natural complete homotopy classification for all finite connected subgraphs of the planar honeycomb lattice, including nonregular patches, cuts, holes and arbitrary bond defects. It identifies a primitive integral persistence kernel and sharp local edge-deletion rank changes: a shared-edge loss transforms two local two-spheres into one essential circle, a topological effect not predicted by prior closed-period or disjoint-hexagon theorems.
